learn.hook: Why does a sharp knife cut a tomato easily while a blunt one squashes it? Same push, very different pressure!
points: Pressure is the force acting on a unit area: pressure = force ÷ area. Its SI unit is the pascal (Pa); 1 Pa = 1 N per square metre.
The same force on a smaller area gives more pressure. That is why knives are sharp and nails are pointed, while school bags have wide straps.
Liquids press on the bottom and sides of their containers. Liquid pressure increases with depth, so water spurts farthest from the lowest hole in a bottle.
Air also has weight and presses on everything in all directions. This is atmospheric pressure; at sea level it is about 1,01,325 Pa (roughly 1 lakh pascal).
Air pressure decreases as we go higher, which is why ears may 'pop' on a drive up to the hills or in an aeroplane.

example.q: Think it through: A force of 200 N acts on an area of 4 square metres. What is the pressure?
steps: Pressure = force ÷ area

learn.reallife: Dams are built much thicker at the bottom than at the top because water pressure is greatest at the bottom.

games.title: More pressure or less?

quiz.q: What is the SI unit of pressure?
quiz.explain: Pressure is measured in pascals; 1 pascal is 1 newton of force on 1 square metre.
steps: Pressure is force per unit area
It is measured in pascals; 1 Pa = 1 N on 1 square metre
Answer: Pascal
quiz.mistake: Confuses the unit of pressure with the unit of force

quiz.q: A force of 300 N acts on 6 square metres. What is the pressure in pascals?
steps: Pressure = force ÷ area
Answer: 50
quiz.explain: We divide force by area to get pressure.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies force by area instead of dividing

quiz.q: The same 60 N force acts on each of these areas. Which area, in square metres, gives the GREATEST pressure?
steps: Pressure = force ÷ area
60 ÷ 0.5 = 120 Pa, the largest of the four
Answer: 0.5
quiz.explain: The smaller the area, the greater the pressure for the same force.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger area gives more pressure

quiz.q: Why does a school bag have wide straps?
options: To increase pressure on the shoulders
To spread the weight over a larger area and reduce pressure
quiz.explain: A larger area means less pressure, so the bag hurts less.
steps: Pressure = force ÷ area
Wide straps spread the bag's weight over a larger area, so the pressure on the shoulders is less
Answer: To spread the weight over a larger area and reduce pressure
quiz.mistake: Does not link area with pressure

quiz.q: Water spurts out of three holes at different heights in a bottle. Which hole sends water the farthest?
quiz.explain: Liquid pressure increases with depth, so the bottom hole has the greatest pressure.
steps: Liquid pressure increases with depth
The bottom hole has the greatest pressure, so its water goes farthest
Answer: The bottom hole
quiz.mistake: Thinks liquid pressure is the same at all depths

quiz.q: Why is a dam wall made thicker at the bottom?
options: Water pressure is greatest at the bottom
Air pressure is greatest at the top
quiz.explain: Deeper water presses harder, so the base must be strongest.
steps: Deeper water presses harder
So the dam's base must be the strongest, because water pressure is greatest at the bottom
Answer: Water pressure is greatest at the bottom
quiz.mistake: Does not know liquid pressure increases with depth

quiz.q: In which direction does air exert pressure?
quiz.explain: Air presses on surfaces from every direction, which is why a sealed balloon stays round.
steps: Air presses on surfaces from every direction
That is why a sealed balloon stays round
Answer: In all directions
quiz.mistake: Thinks air presses only downward

quiz.q: Why do ears sometimes 'pop' when travelling up a hill road to Mussoorie?
options: There is more oxygen up there
quiz.explain: Higher up, outside air pressure is lower than the pressure inside the ear, until they balance with a 'pop'.
steps: Air pressure decreases with height
As we climb, outside pressure falls below the pressure inside the ear, until they balance with a 'pop'
Answer: Air pressure decreases with height
quiz.mistake: Thinks air pressure increases with height

teach.ask: Gappu pecks a mango with a blunt beak and a sharp beak: Why does the sharp one go in more easily? What is pressure?
teach.praise: Pressure is force divided by area. A sharp beak has a tiny area, so the pressure is big. Mango time!
teach.nudge: Pressure depends on the force, but what else? What happens when the area is small?

revise.summary: Pressure = force ÷ area, measured in pascals. The same force on a smaller area gives more pressure (sharp knives, wide bag straps). Liquid pressure increases with depth. Air presses in all directions; atmospheric pressure is about 1,01,325 Pa at sea level and falls with height.
focus: Pressure = force ÷ area and the pascal
Effect of area: knives, nails, bag straps
Air pressure in all directions, decreasing with height
remember: Atmospheric pressure at sea level ≈ 1,01,325 Pa
Dams are thicker at the bottom because pressure rises with depth
traps: Smaller area means more pressure, not less
Air pressure decreases, not increases, as you go higher
The newton is the unit of force, not pressure

learn.hook: On a hot afternoon at Marina Beach in Chennai, a cool breeze blows in from the sea. By night it turns around. Why does the wind change sides?
points: Wind is moving air. Air moves from a region of high pressure to a region of low pressure. The bigger the pressure difference, the faster the wind.
Warm air expands, becomes lighter and rises. Cooler air moves in to take its place. This creates wind.
Land heats up and cools down faster than water. By day, land is warmer, so a sea breeze blows from sea to land. By night, land is cooler, so a land breeze blows from land to sea.

Uneven heating on a huge scale drives the monsoon. In summer the land of India becomes very hot, and moist winds from the oceans blow in and bring the rains (the south-west monsoon, mainly June to September).
Fast-moving air has lower pressure. Strong winds over a roof can lower the pressure above it so that a weak roof may lift off.

example.q: Think it through: You hold a strip of paper below your lips and blow over its top. The strip rises. Why?
steps: Blowing makes the air above the strip move fast.
Fast-moving air has lower pressure.
The still air below has higher pressure and pushes the strip up.
example.answer: The pressure above the strip is lowered by the fast-moving air, so the higher pressure below pushes it up.

learn.reallife: Farmers across India watch for the monsoon's arrival because most of the country's yearly rain falls in these months. A wind vane shows wind direction and an anemometer measures wind speed.

items: Wind blows from high pressure to low pressure.
Air always moves towards the region of lower pressure.
Warm air sinks and cool air rises.
It is the other way round: warm air rises and cool air sinks.
A land breeze blows from land to sea at night.
At night the land is cooler, so air over it has higher pressure.
Land heats up more slowly than water.
Land heats up and cools down faster than water.

quiz.q: Wind blows from:
quiz.explain: Air is pushed from where pressure is higher to where it is lower.
steps: Air is pushed from where pressure is higher
to where it is lower, so wind blows from high to low pressure
Answer: High pressure to low pressure
quiz.mistake: Reverses the direction of wind flow

quiz.q: What happens to air when it is heated?
quiz.explain: Warm air expands, becomes lighter and rises, letting cooler air flow in.
steps: Heated air expands and becomes lighter
So it rises, and cooler air flows in
Answer: It expands and rises
quiz.mistake: Thinks warm air sinks

quiz.q: During a sunny day at the seaside, the breeze usually blows:
options: From the land to the sea
From the sea to the land
quiz.explain: By day land is hotter, air over it rises, and cooler air from the sea moves in.
steps: By day the land is hotter and air over it rises
Cooler air from the sea moves in, so the breeze blows from the sea to the land
Answer: From the sea to the land
quiz.mistake: Mixes up sea breeze and land breeze

quiz.q: Why does the land breeze blow at night?
options: Land cools faster than the sea
The sea cools faster than land
quiz.explain: At night the land is cooler, so the warmer air over the sea rises and air flows from land to sea.
steps: At night the land cools faster than the sea
Warmer air over the sea rises, so air flows from land to sea
Answer: Land cools faster than the sea
quiz.mistake: Thinks water cools faster than land

quiz.q: In India, the south-west monsoon mainly brings rain during:
quiz.explain: The south-west monsoon usually arrives in Kerala around the start of June and brings rain until about September.
steps: The south-west monsoon reaches Kerala around early June
It brings rain until about September
Answer: June to September
quiz.mistake: Does not know the monsoon season

quiz.q: Which instrument measures wind speed?
quiz.explain: An anemometer's cups spin faster in stronger winds. A barometer measures air pressure.
steps: An anemometer's cups spin faster in stronger winds
So it measures wind speed; a barometer measures air pressure
Answer: Anemometer
quiz.mistake: Confuses the anemometer with the barometer

quiz.q: During a storm, a weak tin roof may lift off. Why?
options: Fast wind above lowers the pressure, and the higher pressure below pushes up
The roof becomes lighter in rain
Hot air sinks on to the roof
quiz.explain: Fast-moving air has lower pressure, so the still air inside pushes the roof upward.
steps: Fast wind above the roof lowers the pressure there
The higher pressure of the still air below pushes the roof up
Answer: Fast wind above lowers the pressure, and the higher pressure below pushes up
quiz.mistake: Does not know that fast-moving air has lower pressure

quiz.q: What causes winds on a large scale over the Earth?
options: Uneven heating of the Earth's surface
The Earth being perfectly the same temperature everywhere
quiz.explain: Different places heat up differently, creating pressure differences that make air move.
steps: Different places heat up differently
This creates pressure differences, so uneven heating of the Earth causes winds
Answer: Uneven heating of the Earth's surface
quiz.mistake: Does not link uneven heating with wind

teach.ask: Gappu's feathers ruffle: Where does the wind come from? Why does it blow at all?
teach.praise: Heated air rises, the pressure drops, and air rushes from high pressure to low pressure. That rush is wind. Whoosh!
teach.nudge: Which way does air move between high and low pressure? And what does heating do to air?

revise.summary: Wind is air moving from high to low pressure; warm air expands and rises while cooler air moves in. Land heats and cools faster than water, giving a sea breeze by day and a land breeze by night. Uneven heating drives the south-west monsoon (June to September). Fast-moving air has lower pressure.
focus: High to low pressure and rising warm air
remember: Day: sea breeze (sea → land); night: land breeze (land → sea)
South-west monsoon: mainly June to September
Anemometer measures wind speed; barometer measures air pressure
traps: Wind does not blow from low to high pressure
Land, not sea, cools faster at night
Fast-moving air has lower, not higher, pressure

learn.hook: Weather scientists can now spot a cyclone days before it reaches the coast. Their warnings help millions of people get to safety in time!
points: Thunderstorms often form on hot, humid days when warm, moist air rises quickly, forms tall clouds and brings lightning, thunder, strong winds and heavy rain.
A cyclone forms over warm ocean water. Moist air rises, creating a region of very low pressure, and winds spiral in around it at high speed. The calm centre is called the eye.
The same kind of storm is called a hurricane near the Americas and a typhoon in the western Pacific. In India, more cyclones form in the Bay of Bengal than in the Arabian Sea.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) tracks cyclones with satellites and radar and issues warnings. Coastal states run cyclone shelters and evacuation plans.

Cyclone safety: follow official warnings, keep an emergency kit (water, dry food, torch, first-aid, charged phone, documents), move to a shelter if told, stay indoors, keep away from fallen wires, and fishermen should not go to sea.

example.q: Think it through: Lightning flashes and you are playing in an open ground. A tall, lonely tree stands nearby. Should you shelter under it?
steps: Lightning tends to strike tall objects.
A lonely tree in an open field is the tallest object around.
Shelter in a proper building or a closed car instead; if there is none, crouch low away from trees and poles.
example.answer: No. Move into a building quickly. If you cannot, crouch low in the open, away from tall trees and poles.

learn.reallife: Odisha's early warnings and cyclone shelters have helped move lakhs of people to safety before powerful cyclones, saving many lives.

quiz.q: Where do cyclones form?
quiz.explain: Warm ocean water supplies the heat and moisture that power a cyclone.
steps: A cyclone needs heat and moisture
Warm ocean water supplies both, so cyclones form over warm ocean water
Answer: Over warm ocean water
quiz.mistake: Does not know that cyclones need warm seas

quiz.q: What is the calm centre of a cyclone called?
quiz.explain: The eye is a calm region of very low pressure surrounded by the strongest winds.
steps: The calm region at the centre of a cyclone
is called the eye, surrounded by the strongest winds
Answer: Eye
quiz.mistake: Does not know the structure of a cyclone

quiz.q: The centre of a cyclone has:
quiz.explain: Rising warm, moist air leaves very low pressure at the centre, and winds rush in around it.
steps: Warm, moist air rises at the centre
This leaves very low air pressure there, and winds rush in around it
Answer: Very low air pressure
quiz.mistake: Thinks the centre of a storm has high pressure

quiz.q: Which organisation issues cyclone warnings in India?
quiz.explain: The IMD tracks storms using satellites and radar and issues warnings.
steps: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) tracks storms with satellites and radar
It issues the cyclone warnings
Answer: India Meteorological Department
quiz.mistake: Does not know which agency forecasts weather

quiz.q: In which sea near India do more cyclones form?
quiz.explain: The Bay of Bengal has more cyclones than the Arabian Sea, which is why the east coast faces them more often.
steps: More cyclones form in the Bay of Bengal than in the Arabian Sea
So India's east coast faces them more often
Answer: Bay of Bengal
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Arabian Sea has more cyclones

quiz.q: During a thunderstorm, which is the SAFEST place to be?
quiz.explain: A building protects you from lightning. Tall trees, open fields and water are dangerous.
steps: Lightning strikes tall objects and open spaces; water is dangerous too
A building protects you, so inside a building is safest
Answer: Inside a building
quiz.mistake: Thinks a tree is good shelter in lightning

quiz.q: Which item is most useful in a cyclone emergency kit?
quiz.explain: Power often fails in cyclones, so a torch, water, dry food, first-aid and a charged phone matter most.
steps: Power often fails during cyclones
So a torch with spare batteries is most useful, along with water, dry food and first-aid
Answer: A torch with spare batteries
quiz.mistake: Does not think about practical needs during power cuts

quiz.q: A cyclone near the Americas is usually called a:
quiz.explain: Hurricane is the name used near the Americas; typhoon is used in the western Pacific. A tsunami is caused by undersea earthquakes, not winds.
steps: The same storm has different names in different regions
Near the Americas it is a hurricane; in the western Pacific, a typhoon
Answer: Hurricane
quiz.mistake: Confuses cyclones with tsunamis or monsoons

teach.ask: Gappu trembles: The radio says a cyclone is coming to our coast! What is a cyclone, and how do we stay safe?
teach.praise: A cyclone is a giant spinning storm with low pressure, born over warm seas. We follow warnings and go to a shelter. I feel ready!
teach.nudge: What kind of pressure is at a cyclone's centre? Where does it form? And what should we do when there is a warning?

revise.summary: Thunderstorms form when warm, moist air rises fast. Cyclones form over warm oceans around a calm, very low-pressure eye; they are hurricanes near the Americas and typhoons in the western Pacific. In India the Bay of Bengal has more cyclones, and the IMD issues warnings.
focus: The eye and low pressure at the centre
Names in different regions; Bay of Bengal versus Arabian Sea
IMD warnings and cyclone and lightning safety
remember: Cyclone centre (eye): calm, very low pressure
Hurricane: near the Americas; typhoon: western Pacific
IMD issues cyclone warnings; keep a torch, water, dry food, first-aid, charged phone
traps: Never shelter under a lone tall tree in lightning
A tsunami is caused by undersea earthquakes, not winds
The cyclone's centre has very low, not high, pressure
